headline: The magnetic sub-test was not the clean test either side registered, and one of our own pre-registered falsifiers (OBS-O-02) fired to say so. The dome's own Kp<2 precondition failed (Kp 2.333 for 18-21 UT), and so did its own quiet test (Boulder Z daily stdev 7.62 nT against its < 5 nT rule - a well-defined statistic whose published values we reproduce exactly; no day of July-August 2026 passed it). Evaluated anyway under one post-hoc detectability rule applied to both sides, each registration on the component it names. On Z, the dome's Tier-1 instrument, its signature contact-phase timing is absent at all six priority stations - detectable at the claimed size for every pulse width tried, and at the formula's smaller per-station sizes for widths up to 10 min. Its revised -17 to -21 nT prediction (the formula with its x1.672 correction applied once) is absent at every station above 80% coverage and, jointly across eight stations, at >= 3.8 control-calibrated standard deviations. The uncorrected formula's smaller amplitudes are disfavoured but not robustly excluded. The PRED-095 card itself (-17.8 +/- 2 nT at Ebro or San Pablo, falsified by an H anomaly within +/-3 nT of zero) met neither line on the raw reading: the H anomaly was -9.6 and -12.6 nT (only the tau-0 eclipse-attributable fit at one station each falls inside +/-3 nT). The same rule falsifies the upper part of our own registered -5 to -25 nT band, and as pre-registered that band was met on the eclipse day and on 17 of 30 ordinary days - non-diagnostic, our design error. Our pre-registered binary latitude profile for WIN-010 failed - our error. A latitude-ordered negative Z residual at about half the formula's amplitude coincided with the eclipse (larger than on any of 19 ordinary days); its cause is unresolved, and the dome's FSF ordering fits it only modestly better than a flat profile; with ephemeris coverage a solar-elevation weighting - what standard physics expects for a sunset eclipse - fits it better still. Our Hartland obscuration claim (88%) failed; the true value was 94.4% - our error (erratum ECLIPSE-2026-08-12-ERRATUM-1). The geometric result (294 km path vs the dome's 1.3 km) stands.

SR-1_kp_gate.text: One rule for both sides. Every pre-registered criterion that carries a Kp<2 precondition - ours (B1-M-001, OBS-D-02, OBS-D-04, OBS-S-02) and the dome's (PRED-095 'IF Kp<2', Tier-1 'falsification only on verified Kp<2 day', Tier-3 'Kp<2 entire Aug 9-12', live countdown 'Requires Kp < 2') - is formally UNTESTED: GFZ definitive Kp was 2.333 for 18-21 UT on 2026-08-12 and 3.0 for 15-18 UT on 2026-08-11. Note the dome text also leaves Kp 2-3 unspecified: 'IF Kp >= 3, signal will be buried in storm noise (not a falsification)' (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:74) while validity requires Kp<2 (:91); 2.333 falls in the gap.
SR-1_kp_gate.note: Applies preconditions that WERE pre-registered (ours in the frozen file, the dome's in its published text); the post-hoc part is the decision to apply them identically to both sides.

DR-1_detectability_override.text: Beyond the formal status, a prediction is scored 'as-if' ONLY for the part of its predicted amplitude that exceeds 3 x the empirical null SD of the same metric on the same UT window, estimated from the preceding 30 days with Kp(12-24 UT) <= 3 (i.e. at noise levels comparable to or worse than the eclipse day). The same rule is applied to our ranges and to the dome's. Below that threshold a claim is 'untested at this noise level', not confirmed and not falsified. Detection power for a -17 nT signal was checked by injection into real control-day noise (per-station table in z_component_evaluation).
DR-1_detectability_override.note: Post hoc. Kept physically separate from the scoring of pre-registered criteria; never re-words a frozen criterion.
DR-1_detectability_override.rev3_sensitivity: Threshold varied 2/3/5 sigma in z_component_evaluation.sensitivity_table. The contact-phase conclusion survives every variant; the obscuration-shaped conclusion at -17 nT survives 2 and 3 sigma at all six priority stations and weakens at 5 sigma (power 0.24 at HAD, 0.56 at ESK, 0.58 at EBR).
DR-1_detectability_override.rev4_vocabulary: C3-9: rev4 uses one word for both sides. 'Falsified as-if' (dome entries, predictions.json enum) and our own bands get the same word; rev3's 'refuted' for our side is retired.

DQ-1_publication_state.text: A station is excluded from every absolute-baseline (protocol-metric) criterion if the 16-20 UT median H of its quiet-day set spans more than 50 nT (about 3x the largest span, 16 nT, at any station). Only GUI trips it (~185 nT step between July quasi-definitive and August variation files). Applied uniformly to OBS-D-02 counts, PRED-095 tallies, B1-M-001, B2-M-001/002 and OBS-O-01. Offset-immune template fits are unaffected and are still reported for GUI.
DQ-1_publication_state.note: Post hoc. Kept physically separate from the scoring of pre-registered criteria; never re-words a frozen criterion.

CTL-1_control_stations.text: Any candidate eclipse feature is checked against non-eclipsed observatories with the SAME template and window: ASC (Ascension, zero obscuration, Sun 13 to -1 deg over 18-19 UT, dayside), KOU (Kourou, zero obscuration, full daylight), HER (Hermanus, zero obscuration, NIGHT side after ~16:15 UT - correcting the cycle-1 review, which described HER as dayside). A feature that a non-eclipsed control reproduces at similar z is not attributed to the eclipse.
CTL-1_control_stations.note: Post hoc. Kept physically separate from the scoring of pre-registered criteria; never re-words a frozen criterion.

REV3-SENS_sensitivity_variants.text: Rev3 variants: contact-phase Gaussian width sigma in {3,5,10,20,30} min (rev2 used 10 only; the dome never specified a pulse width); joint-fit trend linear or quadratic (rev2 used linear only); detection threshold 2/3/5 sigma.

REV3-PWR_formula_amplitude_power.text: Injection power computed for the dome formula's own per-station amplitudes (baseline x published coverage x published FSF, BOU -10.9 and W004 -22.24 nT; and BOU with our ephemeris obscuration) as well as the PRED-095 range, at 2/3/5 sigma.

REV4-JOINT_calibrated_amplitude_test.text: Formula amplitude is tested jointly across the 8 evaluable dome-cited stations: residual_s = (A_s - null_mean_s)/(-10.9 x coverage_s), WLS-fitted as k x FSF_s (k = 1: -10.9 baseline; k = 1.672: the x1.672 specification). Distance from k = 1 / 1.672 is expressed in units of the control-day spread of k (19 control days, same statistic), not the WLS se, because station noise is spatially correlated. Three spread estimators are reported (SD, SD without the most extreme control day, 1.4826 x MAD). A specification counts as rejected only if it is >= 3 units away in every trend/lag/coverage variant and under every estimator.

REV4-COMPONENT_named_component_rule.text: Each registration is scored on the component it names: the PRED-095 card on H at EBR/SPT (its falsification line), the dome's 'revised prediction for 12 August' paragraph and Tier 1 on Z (03-predictions.txt:72 'Z minimum', :107 'Z-component'), our B1-M-001 on H (frozen sign_convention). Results on the other component are reported as checks only.

It would not have done so in 2019-2021. We report both; we do not use either reading to score a prediction.

methods.data: INTERMAGNET 1-minute data via BGS GIN web service (https://imag-data.bgs.ac.uk/GIN_V1/GINServices, publicationState=best-avail, per-day requests), 2026-07-13..2026-08-12. H = recorded H, or sqrt(X^2+Y^2) for XYZ-reporting observatories. Fetched 2026-09-26.
methods.obscuration: Computed, not taken from the NASA web calculator: skyfield 1.55 + JPL DE421 topocentric apparent Sun/Moon, WGS84 station coordinates from IAGA-2002 headers, area-overlap of the solar disc at 1-min cadence 15:00-21:00 UT. Validation: greatest eclipse reproduced at 17:45 UT at 65.225N/25.228W with obscuration 1.0 (NASA 17:45:53.8); 2017-08-21 Boulder max at 17:46 UT, 93.6% (matches published local circumstances within ~1 pp). Deviation from the protocol (which named the NASA local-circumstances calculator) is disclosed; an independent NASA-calculator cross-check is recommended before publication.
methods.quiet_days: Protocol step 2 read as: days with max 3-h Kp <= 1 in the 30 days preceding the event, ties/fill by lowest daily Kp sum. Only 4 days satisfy max Kp<=1 (07-19, 07-20, 08-01, 08-06); 5th filled with 08-05 (sum 3.33). Sensitivity set ranked purely by daily sum: 08-06, 08-05, 08-07, 07-19, 08-01. Baseline = per-UT-minute mean over quiet days (finer than the protocol's "same UT-hour"; the difference is sub-nT for this window).
methods.protocol_metric: Peak = max |signed deviation| in +/-60 min around each station's computed max-coverage minute (exact protocol step 2).
methods.supplementary_metric_NOT_PREREGISTERED: Eclipse-isolating detrend: fit a line to the deviation over [first contact-60 min, first contact] and [last contact, last contact+60 min], subtract, report mean residual over [t_max-30, t_max+30]. Empirical null = the same statistic on the same UT windows on every non-quiet day of the preceding 30 days with Kp(15-21UT) <= 2.67 (n=13-19 per station). Sensitivity: anchor 30 vs 60 min, linear vs quadratic.
methods.components: H (our frozen protocol's component) AND Z (the dome's named Tier-1 instrument, monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:107). Both use the same quiet-day per-minute baseline. X/Y/F are available in the scripts but not scored (the dome's pattern clause is moot once amplitude fails).
methods.quiet_days_interpretation: 'Kp <= 1' in protocol step 2 is read as max 3-h GFZ Kp <= 1.0; 1+ (1.333) does NOT qualify. Four days satisfy it (07-19, 07-20, 08-01, 08-06); 08-05 (max Kp 1.333 in 12-24 UT but lowest daily sum 3.33 among the rest) fills the fifth slot per the tie/fill rule. EBR, CLF, BEL and SFS use 4 days because their 2026-08-01 files contain no valid samples 15-21 UT (data gaps); no day was dropped for publication state.
methods.leave_one_out: For control-day statistics the day being evaluated is removed from its own baseline (leave-one-out) so quiet days are not compared with themselves.
methods.joint_template_fit_NOT_PREREGISTERED: Replaces the cycle-1 window-mean detrend as the primary eclipse-isolating metric (the window-mean compared a mean to peak predictions and attenuated lagged signals). Model over [local C1-60, local C4+60]: dev(t) = a + b t + A s(t), with s(t) a template normalised to peak 1, so A is directly a PEAK-equivalent amplitude in nT with the trend fitted simultaneously. Templates: obscuration(t) passed through a first-order recovery lag tau = 0, 15, 30, 60 min; local C1/C4 contact-phase (Gaussians, sigma 10 min, at each station's own first and last contact); global C1/C4 contact-phase (16:59 and 21:01 UT, the contact times in the dome's own post_eclipse_analysis() code, monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:191-195), window 15:59-22:01. Injection into real control-day noise recovers A at 100% for all tau (linear model).
methods.window_mean_detrend_retained_as_sensitiv: The cycle-1 metric is kept only as a sensitivity check. Injection-recovery of its window mean (signal peak-normalised): 100% at tau 0, 95% at 15 min, 83% at 30 min, 61% at 60 min; window-mean/peak ratio ~0.65-0.72. The pre-contact-only extrapolation variant has null SD 6-15 nT and is non-informative (table in per_station).
methods.correlation_tests: Pearson r between the linearly-detrended deviation and each template over the same windows, reproducing the dome's r > 0.7 (success) / r > 0.5 (falsification) thresholds, with the same statistic computed on every control day for a false-positive rate.

lag_mismatch_injection.purpose: C3-4. Does the trend model absorb an eclipse response whose lag differs from the fitted template? Post hoc.
lag_mismatch_injection.method: A response = A x first-order-relaxation(obscuration, lag L) is injected into the real Z deviation of every null day and fitted with the tau-0 and tau-30 templates; recovered fraction = fitted/injected, mean over null days, mean over the six priority stations (station range in the output).
lag_mismatch_injection.reading: With the tau-0 template a response lagged by 15/30/60 min is recovered at 0.817/0.549/0.299 of its peak with a quadratic trend versus 0.945/0.771/0.52 with a linear trend (the curmudgeon's synthetic estimate was 0.75/0.58/0.32 vs 0.94/0.82/0.56). The quadratic variant therefore recovers 14-42% less of a 15-60 min lagged response than the linear variant. The tau-30 template with a quadratic trend is the most lag-robust variant (0.914-1.0 for lags 15-60 min, 0.547 at lag 0). Consequences: quadratic-variant consistency_z values against dome amplitudes are inflated for lagged responses, and 'with a quadratic trend they vanish' is not evidence that nothing eclipse-related was there. Both directions are weakened.

position_dependent_sign_check.purpose: HNOTE item 1. A standard-physics eclipse response need not have one sign at every station (it depends on position relative to the shadow and to the Sq current focus, and on local time). Re-read every rev3 template fit two-sided and compare with a crude local Sq-weakening expectation.
position_dependent_sign_check.sq_proxy: Quiet-day mean of the component at each station's maximum-coverage minute minus its local 00-03 h mean; a first-order Sq-weakening response is expected with the OPPOSITE sign. Crude: it ignores current redistribution around the shadow, induction and the sunset terminator. Post hoc.
position_dependent_sign_check.result: Z: no station shows a positive eclipse-window Z response (largest z +1.04, NGK); the proxy expects positive dZ only at GUI (south of the path, Sq-Z level -4.85 nT), where the fits are weakly negative. So the one-signed Z-down templates did not discard a real positive response at any station on this day. H: the proxy expects small negatives everywhere at this local time (Sq-H level 0.2-1.5 nT at EBR/SPT/CLF/HAD - near its night level at sunset - and 8-12 nT at ESK/LER); one NGK quadratic variant is significantly positive (z +3.61), the rest are not significant.
position_dependent_sign_check.consequences: Dome claims: the dome's registrations specify one sign (Tier 1: 'Z down'; formula: negative anchor) - scored one-sided on its own terms; nothing changes. The local Sq proxy fits the Z residual pattern poorly in the primary variant (chi2 20.0 vs FSF 3.96), mainly because GUI does not flip sign; it fits best only in the tau-30 quadratic variants. Our side: the frozen sign_convention asserted one negative H sign for all stations. That was our representation shortcut (failure_attribution analyst_representation if it had mattered); on this day the proxy agrees with a negative H sign, so no outcome changes. The proxy does say the expected H effect at EBR/SPT near sunset is ~1 nT or less, which is the physical reason our -5 to -25 nT B1-M-001 band was wrong for this geometry (erratum E-3).

kernel_of_truth: Three real things sit under the dome's eclipse claims. Eclipses do disturb ground magnetometers, and on 2026-08-12 the raw H at the dome's stations really was 13-19 nT low. The dome's quiet-day precondition is good practice; its Boulder statistic is well defined and exactly reproducible, and this day failed it. And across the dome's stations the eclipse-window Z residuals do increase northward in its FSF order, more than on any of 19 ordinary days. None of that saves the claims: ordinary days produce the same raw H; the PRED-095 card's H anomaly met neither its claim nor its falsifier; the dome's own named component shows the latitude ordering at about half the formula's -10.9-baseline size and far below its x1.672 size; the contact-phase signature it calls ECM-unique is absent where it would have stood out; and a sunset eclipse under standard Sq physics also produces larger effects where the Sun stood higher - in the north. Being right about the ordering does not favour dome physics. A void test is not a confirmation, and the dome's own live scoreboard still reads PENDING.

WIN_010_profile.method: Observed delta_Z = eclipse-attributable Z joint-fit amplitude (A - null_mean), obscuration template tau 0 (tau 30 and quadratic trend as sensitivity), 8 evaluable stations (COI no data; GUI included because the template fit is offset-immune). Baseline -10.9 nT (the W004 baseline only rescales and cannot change the ranking). Each profile is fitted with one free scale k by weighted least squares (weights from each station's null SD); the profile with lower chi2 "tracks more tightly". CGM latitudes from the WIN-010 prose (centred dipole, IGRF-14 2020 pole). Implementation choices (WLS scale fit, chi2 comparison) are post hoc: the registration did not specify a statistic. Rev4 (C3-10): every k quoted in this block now uses ONE null set - the days on which all 8 stations are evaluable with Kp(12-24 UT) <= 3, leave-one-out - the same set as the control-day comparison. result_Z (rev3, per-station nulls) is kept for the record; result_Z_rev4 is the comparable statistic.
WIN_010_profile.result_Z_summary: Rev3 (per-station nulls): FSF k = 0.524, k/se 4.51, chi2 4.77 vs 13.39 for our binary profile. Rev4 (single null set): FSF k = 0.52, k/se 4.32, chi2 3.96 vs 11.18 for our binary profile. Our binary profile is disfavoured at every alpha and under both coverage inputs: ESK and LER carry the LARGEST negative residuals, not suppressed ones. Rev3 added 'by our own pre-registered rule the discrimination is robust'; that misread the rule - the alpha rule tests whether the linear-coverage approximation is adequate, not whether the discrimination is diagnostic (C3-3e). Withdrawn.
WIN_010_profile.result_H_summary: On H (check): non-discriminating - the winner flips with the metric variant (binary profile wins tau 0 linear; FSF wins with a quadratic trend on all 8 stations but not on the discriminating subset; binary wins tau 30), and the eclipse-day statistics sit inside the control-day distribution.

controls.control_days: Same test on the 19 control days (single null set): FSF k exceeds the event on 0 of 19 (event rank 1 of 20, ~1.8 control SD above the control mean; k/se 4.32, 1 of 19 control days with |k/se| >= that). The PROFILE PREFERENCE is not unusual: delta-chi2(binary - FSF) on the event is 7.22 and 2 of 19 control days equal or exceed it; FSF wins on 12 of 19 ordinary days (rev3_profile_ctl). The unusual quantity is the AMPLITUDE of the latitude-ordered residual, not the profile ranking.

time_shift_demoted_to_limit.reading: Rev3 used the +120 min shift (k/se -6.31) to deny eclipse attribution and omitted +180 (0.99). Calibrated on the same 19 control days, the only CLEAN shifts (no overlap with any station's eclipse 17:02-19:45 UT, not containing the dome global C4 21:01) are pre-eclipse: -240/-300/-360 min give k/se -0.68/-1.13/0.07, unremarkable (10/8/19 of 19 control days at least as large). No post-eclipse window can be made clean within the UT day: +120 and +180 overlap station eclipses, the sunset terminator and 21:01. +120 is unusual on its own (0 of 19 control days), opposite in sign and a poor fit (chi2 25.01); +180 is ordinary (12 of 19). The evening field after the eclipse therefore carries strong latitude-ordered Z structure, but these windows cannot be used either to deny or to grant eclipse attribution. Demoted from evidence to a limit.

WIN_010_profile.scored_result: OUR pre-registered binary magnetic-latitude profile FAILED (failure_attribution analyst_representation): its out-of-band suppression is contradicted, with ESK and LER carrying the largest residuals. A latitude-ordered negative Z residual at ~0.5x the -10.9 formula amplitude (linear trend; 0.167x quadratic) coincided with the eclipse window, larger than on any of 19 control days (~1 in 20). Its cause is NOT ESTABLISHED: eclipse Sq depletion weighted by solar elevation, a storm-recovery external field (Kp 2.333), or chance. Its amplitude disfavours the dome formula at the -10.9 baseline and rejects the x1.672 specification (power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes.joint_amplitude_test). The data do not discriminate FSF from a flat or solar-elevation-weighted profile. Neither side is credited with a physics confirmation; our profile is debited with a failure.
WIN_010_profile.failure_attribution_note: Ours, stated first: the binary <= 30% out-of-band profile was our own first-order stand-in (self-described in the WIN-010 prose as lacking a paper-tabulated attenuation factor; its basis, Kim & Chang, is under the ISS-3101 citation review / erratum E-2). This is a failure of our representation of standard physics, not a demonstrated failure of the Sq mechanism - a solar-elevation profile, the simplest standard expectation for a sunset eclipse, fits nearly as well as FSF (better with ephemeris coverage). The dome is not credited with a confirmation because its FSF profile is not distinguished from flat or solar-elevation profiles and its formula amplitude is not met.
